findings.title: Public findMany API removed without migrating call sites
findings.body: The conversion deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany and changes getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions from Prisma WhereInput objects to Prisma.Sql, but this PR updates no production call sites. Any existing caller using findMany or composing the returned WhereInput objects will fail to compile or break at runtime; callers must be migrated to embed getBaseConditions() in a $queryRaw statement in the same change.

findings.title: Event-type filter fragment is not parenthesized against OR leakage
findings.body: The eventTypeId condition is returned as `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no outer parentheses. It is only safe inside getBaseConditions(), which happens to wrap it; getFilterConditions() is public and if a caller composes it as `WHERE <auth> AND ${filter}` or `${filter} AND <other>`, SQL precedence evaluates it as `a OR (b AND c)`, letting eventTypeId matches bypass the other condition. The fragment itself should be wrapped in parentheses.

findings.title: Array ANY authorization SQL is never actually executed against the database
findings.body: The only $queryRaw execution uses user scope with scalar parameters. The org and team authorization paths, which rely on `"teamId" = ANY(${number[]})` and `"userId" = ANY(${number[]})` parameter binding, are only compared as Prisma.Sql objects with toEqual, so a runtime array-serialization/type error or wrong result from Postgres would pass all tests despite being the highest-risk part of the conversion.

findings.title: Org-scope expectation depends on unspecified database result ordering
findings.body: The test expects teamIds in [org, team, team2, team3] order and userIds in [user, user2, user3] order, but neither findAllByParentId nor MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds guarantees an ORDER BY. The ANY arrays can legitimately be returned in a different order, making this integration test flaky even though the generated SQL is semantically equivalent.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests deleted while caching remains in the service
findings.body: The PR removes the entire Caching describe block, but InsightsBookingService still caches authorization and filter conditions in cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions. Nothing now verifies that repeated calls reuse the cached Prisma.Sql conditions, so a regression in the caching logic (kept through the conversion) would go undetected.
